question: Did Jesus, Mary, and Joseph go to Egypt or Nazareth?
summary: Matthew 2:14 says Joseph fled with Mary and the child to Egypt 'by night' immediately after the magi left. Luke 2:39 says after the temple purification rites — about 40 days after birth, per Lev 12 — they returned directly to Nazareth. The two itineraries cannot both be true: Luke leaves no time for an Egyptian sojourn, and Matthew leaves no room for the temple presentation and Nazareth return before the flight.

reconcile.connective: Gill reads Luke's 'returned to Galilee' as not immediate: the family went back to Bethlehem, awaited the magi, fled to Egypt, then settled at Nazareth.

discrepancy.connective: D. F. Strauss showed neither order works: Luke's forty-day timetable cannot fit the magi, flight, massacre, and return, so at most one series of events actually happened.

skeptic.name: David Friedrich Strauss
skeptic.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
skeptic.attribution: David Friedrich Strauss, The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1835/1846), § 37

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact passage under 'Christ's infancy — order of events' (Matt. ii. 1-23 vs. Luke ii. 4-39), naming Strauss's objection and proposing the harmonizing order: presentation in the temple, then the magi, flight to Egypt, and settlement at Nazareth.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: they returned into Galilee: not that they came from thence to Jerusalem, but from Bethlehem, where Mary gave birth, and her time for purification was now just expired: nor did they go now directly to Galilee; or, if they did, they soon came back again to Bethlehem, since here the wise men found them two years after; when by a divine warning, they went into Egypt, where they remained till Herod's death, and after came into the land of Israel, into the parts of Galilee, and dwelt at Nazareth …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the itinerary tension by reading Luke's 'returned to Galilee' as non-immediate, inserting a return to Bethlehem, the magi's visit, and the Egypt flight before the eventual Nazareth settlement.

And when they had performed all things,.... Relating to the purification of Mary, and the presentation and redemption of her firstborn, and the sacrifices and ceremonies belonging thereunto:
according to the law of the Lord; which that directed to, and enjoined:
they returned into Galilee: not that they came from thence to Jerusalem, but from Bethlehem, where Mary gave birth, and her time for purification was now just expired: nor did they go now directly to Galilee; or, if they did, they soon came back again to Bethlehem, since here the wise men found them two years after; when by a divine warning, they went into Egypt, where they remained till Herod's death, and after came into the land of Israel, into the parts of Galilee, and dwelt at Nazareth; for which reason it is here called their own city,
to their own city Nazareth: Bethlehem was their native city, the place of their birth, at least of their family; and Nazareth was the city of their habitation.
